findings: The alternatives conflate intrinsic camera parameters with physical sensors/end effectors and tool flanges with software technology packages. These category errors do not provide three plausible architecture misconceptions. Replace with parallel, meaningful software/hardware responsibility confusions.

The formula metadata asserts sufficiently independent orientations while this question explicitly repeats the identical orientation/contact pose. The contact/difference equations remain valid without independence; sufficient diversity is a condition for unique recovery, not an assumption satisfied here. Make that condition conditional and retain the rank-deficient case.

The arbitrary flange-point replacement in o1 is not a plausible calibration-verification misconception. Replace it with a meaningful mistaken claim about validation, fitted residuals or reuse of calibration poses.
Option o3 converts a playback multiplier into a calibration-error improvement factor, an unrelated quantity. Use a plausible playback versus physical-motion inference instead.

The incorrect mappings include air ports as object-contact surfaces and fingertips as the actuator housing. These are implausible physical-role assignments rather than competitive gripper component distinctions. Keep all alternatives within meaningful contact, motion, mounting or actuation functions.

Two distractors assert equal friction coefficients on unlike surfaces or that object weight is irrelevant. These implausible absolutes make the qualified answer conspicuous. Use meaningful force-balance assumptions and preserve the source overclaim qualification.

This is a direct conceptual distinction between camera intrinsic/board-pose calibration and robot-frame registration, with no multistep calculation. The present medium label overstates demand; easy is appropriate.

Option o2 infers that two bins in the same coordinate frame must share a destination. This is an implausible category error. Replace it with a competing class-to-bin assignment or image-based selection policy.

The cited p1823/p1824 pixels show corners/ID, PnP and rotation/translation, not the full physical-marker-size and calibrated-camera prerequisites. The official OpenCV evidence supports those added premises, but the lecture citations are mislabeled explicit. Mark their role premise and attach the actual camera-calibration source where appropriate; do not imply the extra prerequisites are printed on these two pages.

Option o1 treats an integer dictionary ID as a translation vector. This type error is not a plausible stage-order alternative. Replace it with a meaningful detection-versus-pose or frame-transform mistake.

The incorrect choices change decimal precision, change units or deliberately reuse arbitrarily old coordinates. They do not meaningfully compete with the sole synchronization protocol. Use plausible but insufficient concurrency/handshake designs under the stated read/write model.
Option o4 divides translations by world-frame coordinates, which is not a meaningful homogeneous-transform cancellation operation. Replace with a plausible factor-order or inverse-placement error.

All three incorrect alternatives invent arbitrary quantitative performance claims (four seconds, ten cycles, sub-mm error). They test absence of logs rather than the depicted cell and leave only one visual option. Include plausible image-grounded alternatives or a meaningful inference distinction.
